acceptedFindings.title: No formal comparison of survival curves
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The objective is to assess how event-free survival differs by treatment group, but the analysis provides only two isolated survival estimates (at different times) without a log-rank test, hazard ratio, confidence intervals, or any measure of difference or uncertainty. The present results cannot address the question.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Perform a log-rank test (or Cox regression) comparing the two groups, report the test statistic, p-value, and appropriate confidence intervals. Include Kaplan-Meier curves with number-at-risk tables and median survival times.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check that stats-run.json contains no test statistic or p-value; verify that estimates are only two point values.

acceptedFindings.title: Critically inadequate survival-analysis reporting
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The manuscript does not report: number of subjects per group, number of events, number censored, total follow-up time, median survival, survival at clinically meaningful time points, or any graphical display of the survival curves. This violates STROBE and CONSORT guidelines for survival data and prevents any clinical interpretation.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Revise the Results section to include the mandatory items: sample size per arm, event counts, censoring pattern, Kaplan-Meier plot, median survival (if reached), and a formal comparison statistic.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Confirm that the current manuscript contains only two undefined survival probabilities and no other survival metrics.

acceptedFindings.title: Missing formal comparison of survival curves
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without a statistical test (e.g., log-rank) we cannot determine if the observed difference between groups is due to chance. The primary question 'How does event-free survival differ by treatment group?' is not addressed.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Compute log-rank test (or Cox proportional hazards model) and report p-value, possibly with a figure showing both curves and a table of comparisons.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check if a p-value for treatment effect is present in the stats-run or manuscript outputs.

acceptedFindings.title: Survival probabilities reported at different follow-up times for each group
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The comparison is invalid: group 0 survival (0.367) at time 493.1 vs group 1 survival (0.000) at time 354.3. Different time points make the difference uninterpretable; the shape of the curves matters.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report survival probabilities at clinically meaningful, fixed time points (e.g., 1-year) or present entire curves with a log-rank test. Summarize with median survival times if appropriate.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check that the reported times for both groups are identical or within a narrow, prespecified window.

acceptedFindings.title: Variables not defined
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The treatment groups (0 and 1) are not described; the event that defines 'event-free survival' is not specified; censoring rules, follow-up origin, and unit of time are unclear. Without these, the study cannot be reproduced or judged for clinical validity.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Explicitly define: (a) the treatment or exposure represented by levels 0 and 1; (b) the composite or single event used for event-free survival; (c) the time origin and censoring rules; (d) how missing data were handled.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Inspect stats-run.json: variables are only 'survival_time', 'event', 'treatment' with no coding information. Manuscript has no definitions.

acceptedFindings.title: No confounding control or adjustment
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The study is observational; treatment groups may differ systematically in prognostic factors. Simple Kaplan-Meier curves without any adjustment or stratification can produce misleading differences that are not causal. The manuscript acknowledges this in the limitations but does not incorporate any mitigating analysis.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: If covariate data are available, perform a Cox regression adjusted for potential confounders (e.g., age, disease severity) and report adjusted hazard ratios. If covariates are absent, discuss the strong potential for confounding and refrain from any causal language.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check that the artifact package contains no covariate information; the variables array in stats-run.json includes only outcome, event indicator, and treatment.

acceptedFindings.title: Complete-case analysis without justification
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The manuscript states the sample size is 240 complete-case records but does not report the original sample size, the amount of missing data, patterns of missingness, or whether missingness is associated with outcome/exposure. Complete-case analysis can yield biased estimates if data are not missing completely at random.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Document the flow from the original cohort to the analytic sample, quantify missingness for each variable, justify the complete-case approach, and consider sensitivity analyses (e.g., multiple imputation) if missingness is substantial.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Verify that no prior cohort-selection or missing-data report exists in the artifact directory.

acceptedFindings.title: Analysis is unbound and exploratory, undermining its evidential value
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The run is marked as 'exploratory_standard_table' with 'unbound' status, meaning no pre-specified method selection or analysis plan governs it. This makes any p-values or inferences potentially post-hoc and increases the risk of selective reporting. The results cannot be promoted to study claims.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Create a formal AnalysisSpec artifact that pre-defines the primary endpoint, comparison method, and sensitivity analyses. Bind the run to that specification and re-run to ensure results are specification-governed.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check binding.status in stats-run.json: 'unbound'; resultPosture is 'exploratory_standard_table'.

acceptedFindings.title: Implausible zero survival in group 1
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The survival estimate for group 1 reaches 0.0 at time 354.29. This could mean all subjects experienced the event, but it is a extreme finding that warrants verification. Without the full curve or at-risk table, we cannot exclude data errors (e.g., all patients censored before that time) or misinterpretation. The claim of zero survival may be incorrect or clinically unlikely.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Examine the raw Kaplan-Meier data (kaplan-meier-curve.csv) and the analytical dataset to confirm that group 1 indeed had events in every subject and no early censoring. Provide the number at risk when survival drops to zero and comment on clinical plausibility.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Inspect estimate for group 1: survival = 0 at time 354.29. Cross-check with the curve CSV to ensure the drop is due to events, not an empty risk set.

acceptedFindings.title: Manuscript conclusion is unsubstantiated
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The Conclusion states 'The analysis produced interpretable local evidence,' but the reported results are two survival probabilities without clinical context, comparison, or error bars. No reader can interpret such data as evidence for or against a treatment difference. This weakens the credibility of the entire report.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Rewrite the conclusion to reflect only what the analysis actually demonstrated (e.g., 'Kaplan-Meier curves were estimated but formal comparison was not performed; therefore, no inference about treatment difference can be drawn.')
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Locate the sentence in the manuscript: 'The analysis produced interpretable local evidence, but methods review is required before stronger claims.' No numeric results support 'interpretable evidence.'

acceptedFindings.title: Manuscript contains false claims about missing estimates and report availability
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Undermines credibility of the manuscript: statements like 'No estimate-like records were available for p-value/effect-size checks' and 'No reader-facing report was available for claim alignment' contradict the presence of estimates and a generated manuscript.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Remove or correct these statements after verifying consistency between the manuscript generator and the actual artifact outputs.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Inspect the Limitations section against the stats-run.json and the manuscript itself; ensure no false denials exist.

acceptedFindings.title: No confidence intervals for survival estimates
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Point estimates without uncertainty measures are misleading. Readers cannot assess precision or compare groups properly.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Compute 95% confidence intervals for each survival estimate (e.g., Greenwood method) and display them in text/tables.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Verify presence of CI columns in the estimates output.

acceptedFindings.title: Missing cohort derivation and missingness details
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The sample size of 240 complete cases suggests exclusion of records with missing data. Without describing initial N, missingness patterns, and reasons for exclusion, results may be biased and are not reproducible.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide a flow chart of inclusion/exclusion, report missingness frequency by variable, and consider sensitivity analysis (e.g., multiple imputation) if missingness is substantial.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check for a table or narrative detailing participants excluded and the final analytic N derivation.

acceptedFindings.title: Variables not defined; unclear treatment groups and event definition
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The meaning of treatment groups 0/1, the event type, and survival time metric are unknown, preventing clinical interpretation and external validity assessment.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add a variables table with definitions, coding, units, and source of each variable (e.g., 'treatment: 0=standard, 1=experimental'; 'survival_time: days from randomization to event/censor'; 'event: 1=death, 0=censored').
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check for a codebook or variable dictionary artifact.

acceptedFindings.title: Analysis is unbound and exploratory, not governed by a pre-specified protocol
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The risk of p-hacking and selective reporting is high; results should not be interpreted as confirmatory evidence. The manuscript does not clearly convey this exploratory status.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Either label the analysis as 'exploratory' with strong caveats, or create/bind a method-selection artifact and analysis specification before rerunning to elevate to a confirmatory posture.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check that the binding fields in stats-run.json are populated and that a pre-registered analysis plan exists.

acceptedFindings.title: Absence of literature review or external context
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Readers cannot assess how these findings fit within existing evidence; the clinical or public health significance is not established.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add a brief background section with relevant citations and discuss how the local results compare to published outcomes.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check for a references or introduction with citations in the manuscript.
